Incident 01 · Downtown Toronto · Night ops

Hold Union Station.

Three infected columns are moving through the real street network. Command from eagle view — or dive to the pavement and fight beside your towers as a survivor in a third-person shooter.

10 wavesHand-tuned escalation from walkers to armoured tanks, with a route gate to breach on every approach.
Two scalesEagle command on the live Mapbox city above; dive and the street fight renders locally, geo-anchored to the street you picked. The simulation never pauses.
100% evacSurvive every wave while the platforms clear. Headshot the armoured leaders to strip a route's armour.
  1. 1Eagle: select a defense below, then click a highlighted lot for ground towers or click a highlighted rooftop for marksmen. Every highlighted spot will place on the first click. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.
  2. 2Dive: press F or the DIVE button to arm a dive, then click anywhere on the map — you land on the nearest road centreline, on the road itself, facing the incoming column. If no road is in reach, the dive refuses and says why. Scrolling all the way down dives at your cursor the same way. P pauses.
  3. 3Street (TPS): click fires (aim locks if your browser allows it). WASD move, Shift sprint, mouse aims over the shoulder, click fires the semi-auto rifle, right-mouse tightens aim, R reloads, Space dodge-rolls, tap F shoves, hold F (or M) ascends and banks your Precision Chain, Q concussion, E decoy.
  4. 4Between waves, draft one upgrade. Watch for blue Intercept Windows — 20-second bonus events on real streets.

Live Mapbox Standard city (dusk — never day) · gameplay geometry from OSM snapshot, 3 Oct 2026 · Fictional scenario

  20. Brief #5 · D1 Street walkers — ROOT CAUSE FOUND: three.js r128 culls an InstancedMesh against its geometry bounding sphere at the mesh origin (one small cylinder at 0,0,0). Eagle view usually keeps the origin in frame, so the horde drew; the street camera looks away from the origin and the ENTIRE horde was culled in one test — the survivor survived only because his meshes already set frustumCulled=false. zombieMesh / head / blob, plus evacuee, car, streetlight, backdrop, placement and street-building instanced meshes, are now frustumCulled=false, re-asserted on hybrid entry. Walkers draw from the shared sim positions every frame in the street renderer, with DOM health bars (shown in street mode) and hitscan against the same positions. QA hooks: __towerDefense.streetProof() stages a walker in front of the survivor; .hybrid() reports zombiesWithin120m, zombieMeshCount and zombieFrustumCulled.

  21. Brief #5 · D2 Balance — INVESTIGATION: Wave 2 composition: 3 Bay + 7 King walkers + 1 armoured leader tank (442 HP) on the busiest route; Wave 3: 3/3/8 walkers+runners + leader. A full wave-2 leak is 10×4 + 22 = 62 station damage — the tester's 68-point drop means nearly everything leaked. Two causes found in the code: (1) tower targeting picked the SMALLEST route distance — the trailer at the back of the column — so leaders walked the full length of tower range unshot; towers now engage the most-progressed walker in range. (2) All routes spawned from one shared queue within ~4 s, so two full columns arrived simultaneously. Barricade/siren effects were verified applying on-route (barricade 14 dmg + 50% slow on hit; siren 5 dmg + 42% slow AoE every 0.58 s tick) — they were being spent on the wrong zombies. Tuning: gates stagger in waves 1–4 (busiest first, next +24 s, third +48 s; +8 s from wave 5), walker HP 44 → 40, barricade damage 12 → 14, marksman damage 42 → 48. Proof Gate 2: selfPlay() now places the canonical Barricade + Siren + Marksmen ($340 of $450) at coverage-best spots near the Union convergence and prints Union HP per wave — the gate is wave 3 ending ≥ 50% and survival to wave 5.

Brief #7 · D1 Cadence finding (from the code): tower attack resolution lives inside the fixed-timestep sim — updateTowers is called only from stepSim, driven by the 20 Hz accumulator; it never resolved per render frame. The actual live-vs-headless couplings were: (1) the accumulator was fed the render dt clamped to 1 s, so frames longer than 1 s silently dropped sim time while wall-clock timers kept running; (2) the route armour-strip timer ran on performance.now() — a headless selfPlay wave finishes in under a second of real time, so the “15 s” strip silently covered the whole headless run while live play lost it after 15 s. Fixes: the accumulator now takes the full real elapsed time (3 s/frame cap, backlog shed only past 600 steps); the armour strip and the decoy lifetime run on state.missionTime like every other sim duration. Combat state now advances only in SIM_DT steps of missionTime — frame rate cannot change tower DPS.
    31. 
          
  31. Brief #7 · D1 Degraded-cadence self-play + wave-2 retune: selfPlay() now runs all three placements (tuned / first-timer chokepoints / Union guard) at BOTH cadences — standard 50 ms steps and degraded 500 ms frame steps (the tester's ~2 FPS conditions, accumulated and burned down in fixed steps exactly as the main loop does) — six runs, gate on the worst: wave-2 leak ≤ 10 pts and wave-3 Union ≥ 50% in every run. Wave 2 King West retuned until it holds at the degraded cadence: King column 7 → 5, wave-2 leader HP ×1.0 → ×0.7 (182), leader gate-chew ×0.55 → ×0.45. Second finding, from the first both-cadences transcript: the tuned placement leaked 12 degraded / 0 standard while the other placements matched exactly across cadences — the sim was drawing unseeded Math.random (spawn laterals, cooldown jitter, event positions), so no two runs ever rolled the same dice and a marginal placement flipped on jitter. selfPlay now runs on a seeded rng — identical dice for all six runs and every click — so a standard-vs-degraded difference, if one ever appears, can only be cadence coupling.

Brief #7 · D2 Scored dive orientation: the LIVE dive path (beginDiveAt — the staging hook is untouched and unused for proof) now picks its heading by score: candidates are the route direction toward the incoming walkers, the street axis both ways, and the route chord both ways; each is scored by clear-ray distance against footprints plus route gates (barriers, at their true 2.9 m beam footprint in the gate's own frame — the first cut's 19 m radius around the gate centre poisoned the correct down-route heading itself; caught and fixed on the Temperance St live dive) plus the Union Station structure. Longest clear ray wins (minimum acceptable 20 m); ties within 2 m break toward the incoming walkers, then by fixed candidate order — fully deterministic. A heading whose 20 m ray is blocked is never chosen when a clear alternative exists. hybrid() now reports diveClearRayM and diveHeadingKind for any real dive; QA hook __towerDefense.diveAt(x, z) performs a real dive at sector-metre coords.

Brief #8 · D1 DIVERGENCE — INSTRUMENTED, THEN FOUND: the game now carries live wave counters (waveStats): sim-seconds vs wall-seconds for the current wave, tower shots fired per type, tower damage dealt, gate damage taken per route, leak points per route — printed on the dev panel every 600 ms, exposed as __towerDefense.waveStats(), and printed by selfPlay for every wave of every run, so harness and live compare line by line. The finding: the sim is cadence-clean — driven through the REAL rAF loop at 500 ms frames with identical placements and identical seeded dice, the live game reproduces the harness transcript exactly. Suspects cleared: (a) the step guard needs 10 steps per 500 ms frame against a 600 cap — nothing drops; (b) no walker movement, gate damage, armour/decoy timing or projectile resolution lives outside stepSim in either path; (c) towers are hitscan in both paths — there is no projectile travel time. The divergence is (d) placement coordinates: all three of brief #7's harness configs put the marksman at the Union convergence (or one tower per gate) — the only distributions that hold. Two equally plausible distributions the harness never tested collapse under the identical sim: marksman at the King chokepoint leaked 26–30 pts on wave 2 and ended wave 3 at 56–58%; marksman at the Yonge chokepoint leaked ~26–30 on wave 2 — the tester's reported 32 pts and 12% sit inside that envelope. The harness was grading placements a player cannot be assumed to pick.

Brief #9 · D1 STREET CLICK ROUTING — fire lives on the canvas, nowhere else: the document-level mouse-up that completed canvas presses anywhere on screen is deleted — there is no window/document fire handler at all. The press is recorded in onPointerDown and the shot resolves in onPointerUp, both bound only to the render canvases: a shot can only originate from a press that began on the street canvas and is released on it with < 7 px total travel (drag-look still accumulates travel via pointer move / lock movement, and a drag that rotated the camera never fires; at any ambiguity the resolution is NOT firing). ASCEND, SEND WAVE and every other HUD element live outside the canvas — their clicks structurally cannot reach the fire path. The canvas mouse-up that remains only releases right-button aim. Brief #9 · D2 DIVE ORIENTATION — ray scoring ABOLISHED, road-anchored spawning: (a) the dive point snaps to the nearest road centreline point within the dive radius (150 m), kept ≥ 6 m from the intersection corners (segment ends); if the snapped point sits inside a footprint, the spawn walks along the centreline until clear — the survivor spawns ON the road. (b) survivor yaw and camera yaw are both set from the road segment's direction vector, signed to face the incoming column (against the route's travel direction when the road carries a route) — computed from road geometry, never from a cast ray. (c) the camera sits on the road behind the survivor at eye height along the same centreline, so the first frame is road + survivor's back + street ahead by construction. (d) the clear-ray survives only as a dev-panel “los log” line — never a gate, never a claim. If no anchor can be satisfied, the dive refuses with “No clear road here — pick another spot” (and the reticle chip says so before you click) instead of landing badly; the dive stays armed for another click.

  44. Brief #9 · D3 EAGLE WALKER GLYPHS — rebuilt on the bolt's path: the separate #walkerGlyphs layer, its 40-cap and its leaders-first dropping logic are deleted. Glyphs now live in #eagleFx — the bolt container — are projected by the same projectToScreen, and update from inside updateEagleFx, the bolt loop, every frame. Visibility rule = the bolts' rule: a walker on screen at altitude ≤ 80 m gets a glyph (≥ 13 px, type colour, health bar), full stop — the pool grows to the on-screen count and the ONLY reduction is clustering: past 60 walkers in frame, walkers sharing a 48 px cell collapse into a cluster badge with the count and the cell's worst health. The expanding-ring impact effect stays.
    45. 
          
  45. Brief #9 · D4 THE FIGHT COMES TO THE DIVE STREET: when the player dives during an active wave, the nearest active column's advance party (3–5 walkers) is re-routed in the sim: each gets a personal detour polyline — current route point → the dive point's road → rejoin its route ~40 m past the dive point — so the party passes the player's position within ~20 s of landing. Positions, targeting and hitscan all flow through the detour-aware path (zombiePos / pathPoint); route distance freezes during a detour (gate siege and leaks stay route-true, and the siege clamp re-takes a walker whose rejoin lands past its gate). The D1 counters name the routed route in the wave line (“routed R2 YONGE ST.”) and the incident feed calls the bend. Between waves nothing is routed — street mode stays free-roam, no fake spawns.
    46. 
          
  46. Brief #9 · D5 YONGE ROUTE — sixth placement + route tuning: the harness gains the Yonge-thin spread (barricade King chokepoint / siren Bay chokepoint / marksmen on an east rooftop, nothing dedicated to Yonge), gated on waves 1–3 with wave-3 total leak ≤ 20; waves 4–5 are reported with draft picks spent (Reinforced Barricades after wave 3, Marksmen Optics after wave 4), not gated. Tuning, chosen against a standalone replica of the column-vs-gate math that reproduces the live 40-point leak exactly at build #8 settings: Yonge gate 170 → 255 and wave-3 Yonge column 7 → 6. Waves 1–2 are untouched — neither has a Yonge column, and the wave-2 leak-0 result stands on all placements.
    47. 
          
  47. Brief #9 · D6 MAPBOX LOAD RETRY: a map error no longer latches the local fallback on first sight. The gate now spends its one retry first — style reload with a visible “Reconnecting to live map…” state in the loading line and the MAP status — and the fallback latches only when the retry has also failed (a second error, or the post-retry 12 s grace expiring, or the standing 25 s style timeout). Once latched, the fallback's behaviour is exactly as before.
